summary: Stevens County peak with 1926 lookout clippings; a second history ties them to Little Blue Grouse in Pend Oreille County instead.

events.note: June 1926 newspaper item names Richard Smith as lookout on Blue Grouse mountain in the Sacheen Lake district. Willhite argues this probably refers to Little Blue Grouse Mountain.
Newport Miner, June 1930: Ernest Hart is to be stationed at Boyer lookout on Blue Grouse Mountain. Willhite says Boyer Mountain was formerly known locally as Blue Grouse Mountain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Weebly page places the 1926 clippings on Blue Grouse Mountain in Stevens County. Willhite argues they more likely describe Little Blue Grouse Mountain in Pend Oreille County, because a 1922 station is recorded there and the 1926 item mentions Sacheen Lake, and says the Stevens County peak is not related. The story reports both views and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Little Blue Grouse Mountain Lookout Site

notes_for_editor: Two peaks share the name, and the record's 1926 clippings may belong to the other one. Willhite's page places a lookout on Little Blue Grouse Mountain (Pend Oreille County, 4,230 ft by its own account), with a 1923 pole tower and cabin, abandoned in the 1930s. Decide whether this record should stay on the Stevens County peak or move to the Little Blue site. The Stevens peak has no source about a structure now. Willhite also says the Little Blue site is reached through a gate that needs a permit and that Inland Empire Paper Company owns the land; I left that out because it may describe the other peak.
